title: ECLIPSE 7.0
description: ECLIPSE 7.0 is the flagship event of the ACM Student Chapter, TIET, and a premier 24-hour hackathon that draws participation from across the nation. As the chapter’s most distinguished and celebrated initiative, it serves as a dynamic platform for developers, designers, and innovators to collaborate and compete. With expert-led workshops, dedicated mentorship, and an intense build environment, ECLIPSE 7.0 is designed to cultivate innovation, enhance technical excellence, and transform ambitious ideas into impactful, real-world solutions. • The hackathon is open to students from all Colleges and Universities. • Students from all academic years are eligible to participate. Teams may include members from different colleges. • Participants from diverse specializations are welcome to form teams together. Teams must consist of 2–5 members. Participants are advised to form teams with complementary expertise, including design, frontend development, backend development, and database management. Each team must choose only ONE problem statement. The detailed problem statements will be published in the PDF below and simultaneously made accessible on the ECLIPSE 7.0 website and ACM’s official social media platforms. Round 1: Pre-Screening Round (Online): Teams will be shortlisted based on their idea presentation. Round 2: Offline Hackathon Round: Shortlisted teams will participate in the on-site hackathon. During the offline round, teams will be assessed at regular checkpoints to ensure consistent progress. All rounds must be completed within the officially communicated timelines. Physical attendance at the venue is mandatory for all qualifying participants. Required submissions for the offline round include: A code repository link and/or deployed project link and a project proposal document • Teams must register exclusively through Devfolio and provide accurate team and member details. • Teams will be evaluated only on the problem statement they have selected. Working on multiple problem statements is strictly prohibited. • The prototype must be developed strictly during the offline round. Pre-built solutions will result in disqualification. • Plagiarism is strictly prohibited and will result in immediate disqualification. • All participants are required to join the official event application and community platform. Failure to comply may result in disqualification. • Any form of misconduct or rule violation may result in disqualification at the discretion of the organizing committee. • Projects will be evaluated by a panel of judges. The decision of the judges will be final and binding. title: haxfinity
description: 12–13 December 2026 10:30 AM, 12 December – 10:30 AM, 13 December Amal College of Advanced Studies (Autonomous), Nilambur, Kerala Prizes:Exciting prizes — details to be announced Team size:2–4 participants Participation: Free Build real solutions, solve meaningful problems, and create something that works. HAXFINITY is a 24-hour hackathon conducted as part of XTHRON ’26, the annual IT fest of the Department of Computer Science, Amal College of Advanced Studies (Autonomous), Nilambur. Students from different colleges and backgrounds will identify problems, build software prototypes, and present their work to judges. The event includes the opening ceremony, a 21-hour project-building window, demonstrations, judging, and awards. There is no compulsory theme. Teams may choose any problem and build a software solution using any suitable technology. Build a product, tool, or prototype that solves a real problem or explores an idea. Build an application using machine learning, generative AI, NLP, computer vision, data analysis, or another AI-related technology. Build technology that improves people’s lives — for example, in education, healthcare, accessibility, sustainability, financial inclusion, or community welfare. Detailed judging criteria will be published before the event. Building window:*11:00 AM, 12 December – 8:00 AM, 13 December (21 hours). Students from all colleges, streams, and experience levels are welcome. You can participate as a beginner, developer, designer, or creative problem-solver. Interests in AI, cybersecurity, web, mobile, cloud, or social-impact technology are all welcome. Amal College of Advanced Studies (Autonomous) Santhigramam, Eranhimangad Nilambur, Malappuram, Kerala — 679329 Check-in and travel details will be shared with registered participants. Opportunity to demo projects to judges Competition Rules All project-specific development must happen during the official building window. Teams may arrive with an idea, but pre-built projects cannot be submitted. Open-source libraries, APIs, datasets, and templates are allowed, subject to their licences. Teams should submit early; late submissions may not be accepted. A working prototype or meaningful demonstration is expected. Teams must be able to explain their technology, process, third-party components, and contributions. Projects must not violate copyright, privacy, security, or applicable law. title: CODERAVE 2.0
description: CODE • COLLABORATE • INNOVATE - The SLIET Annual Hackathon. Organized by Internwell SLIET Club Venue: Sant Longowal Institute of Engineering and Technology (SLIET), Longowal, Punjab Mode: Hybrid — Online (All India) + Offline (SLIET Campus) Coderave 2.0 is a national-level hybrid hackathon designed to bring together innovative minds, passionate developers, designers, and problem-solvers to transform ideas into impactful technology solutions. Organized by Internwell SLIET Club, this edition offers students an opportunity to demonstrate their creativity, technical expertise, teamwork, and problem-solving abilities through a competitive, time-bound development experience. The hackathon welcomes teams from colleges and universities across India through its online participation track, while SLIET students can participate in the offline campus track. Shortlisted teams will present their ideas through PPT pitches, followed by an intensive 24-hour open-source development challenge in which participants will build, test, and demonstrate their solutions. Whether you are interested in web development, app development, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, data science, or other emerging technologies, Coderave 2.0 is your platform to innovate, collaborate, and compete. Round 1 — Registration and PPT Submission: The Team Leader registers the complete team and submits the project proposal PPT. Round 2 — PPT Evaluation and Shortlisting: Judges evaluate submissions based on innovation, problem relevance, feasibility, technical approach, potential impact, and presentation quality. Round 3 — PPT Pitch: Shortlisted online teams(Max 20 team) pitch through an online meeting. Shortlisted SLIET teams pitch offline on campus on 13 February. Round 4 — 24-Hour Open-Source Hackathon: Selected teams(Both online and offline track) build their solutions within the official development window. Round 5 — Final Submission and Evaluation: Teams submit their working solution, source code repository, demo video, and other required deliverables. Judges evaluate the final projects and announce the winners. The hackathon is an opportunity to turn ideas into functional prototypes within 24 hours. Teams are expected to develop their solutions during the official event window and use open-source tools, libraries, and technologies wherever possible. Participants must maintain a project repository, provide clear documentation, and ensure that their work is demonstrable. Teams must disclose third-party components and follow applicable open-source licences. Previously developed work must be declared, and the core solution must comply with the organizers' originality requirements. Exciting prizes, goodies, certificates, and recognition await outstanding teams. Final awards, prize amounts, sponsor benefits, and certificate eligibility will be announced through the official event communication. Note: The dates above are tentative until officially confirmed. The year, registration deadline, online pitch schedule, and final evaluation schedule will be published by the organizers. Bring your idea, build your team, and turn innovation into impact. Register for Coderave 2.0 and take your first step toward creating something extraordinary. title: HACK WITH GDG S4
description: Hack With GDG S4 is the fourth season of the flagship hackathon organized by Google Developer Groups – KSR College of Engineering (GDG KSRCE) . The event brings together developers, designers, innovators, and problem-solvers to transform ideas into impactful solutions through technology. Due to unforeseen circumstances, Hack With GDG S4 has been postponed . The revised dates for the hackathon will be announced soon. Participants are requested to follow our official communication channels for updates regarding the new schedule, submission deadlines, and other event-related announcements. Participants will submit their project idea in PPT/PDF format for evaluation. Teams will be evaluated based on their problem statement, proposed solution, innovation, feasibility, and potential impact. A working prototype is not mandatory at this stage, but prior technical work may be considered an advantage. Selected teams will advance to the offline hackathon. Selected teams will participate in a 36-hour offline hackathon , where they will build and demonstrate their solutions on-site. Hack With GDG S4 welcomes participants across different skill levels and backgrounds. Both beginners and experienced participants are welcome to participate. title: DSH Hacks V2 ($100k+ in prizes!)
description: DSH Hacks V2 is a global student competition open to students aged 13+ hosted collaboratively by three youth-led organizations: DeltaForge Hacks, NXT Horizon, and STEMise. Theme: AI x Healthcare This event brings together young innovators from around the world to transform bold ideas into technical products that address the health challenges facing our world today. Participants will work individually or in teams to identify a real-world healthcare problem and design and develop a meaningful technical solution. Projects may range from diagnostic tools tackling global disease burdens, to patient-care platforms improving access and outcomes, to AI-powered systems reimagining how we detect, treat, and manage illness. Creativity, feasibility, technical depth, clinical insight, and real-world impact will be central to evaluation. The theme of this competition is to build technical solutions that solve pressing healthcare problems. These solutions can be an app, a website, a simulation, a system, or an algorithm. Participants are encouraged to use AI to help them build a meaningful solution and to lower the technical barrier that poses challenges for beginners with ambitious project ideas.

title: QNX Global Hackathon
description: For decades, QNX has been running the systems people bet their lives on, from medical devices and factory floors to trains, robots, and more than 275 million vehicles. It guarantees not just that your code runs, but exactly when. Now QNX 8.0 is free for non-commercial use, and the QNX team wants to see what you do with it when nobody hands you a spec. Build a robot that reacts in microseconds instead of milliseconds. Write the driver nobody has written yet. Port something you love to QNX, or build the tooling you always wished existed. If it runs on QNX 8.0, or helps someone else build for it, it counts. Pick your category and compete for a share of $50,000. Show us what you can do! Why join? Get your hands on a real-time OS, free . QNX Everywhere gives you QNX SDP 8.0, QNX Developer Desktop, and the QNX Hypervisor for non-commercial use, plus free training courses to get you moving. No target hardware required; QEMU works, and so does a Raspberry Pi 5. In 275 million vehicles. Now on your laptop . Not a teaching edition or a stripped-down trial. It's the same QNX that ships in commercial systems, and until QNX Everywhere, building on it meant a commercial license. Compete for $50,000 in prizes . Plus swag, a coffee chat with a QNX exec, and a feature on the QNX blog and social channels. Get Started Get free access to QNX SDP 8.0 through QNX Everywhere (5 minutes) Run through the QNX SDP 8.0 Quick Start Guide and get a program running on your target or QEMU (45 minutes) Browse QNX sample projects and open-source ports , then pick your category (30 minutes)

title: Lean In Hacks 8.0
description: Lean In Hacks is an annual flagship hackathon of Lean In IGDTUW - the first chapter of Lean In India. Lean In Hacks is a beginner-friendly hackathon and has a place for everyone wanting to learn, build, share, and grow in their lives through their unique ideas. Our hackathon journey started in 2020 when we conducted the first edition of Lean In Hacks to give grounds to new thoughts and tools to animate the imaginative and critical thinking side of developers. This time, hackers from any college can participate in our hackathon, which will be held in hybrid mode . The only requirement is to have at least 1 female in your team ! Hackers will be given the weekend to build their product online and the top teams will be given a chance to pitch in the offline mode . As a beginner-friendly hackathon, we offer a dedicated Beginner’s Track exclusively for first-time hackers. This track is designed as an ideathon for first-year students , aimed at fostering innovative thinking, creativity, and confidence in problem-solving. GeNarrative Clash features an Open Track focused on building real-world solutions that assist, elevate, and support creative artists in their work. You are free to solve any real-world problem in the artistic or creative domain.

title: PayPal AI Hackathon
description: About the challenge PayPal already moves money for millions of people and businesses, every day, all over the world. This hackathon is us opening that platform up and asking what happens when you put AI behind the wheel. New agents, new ways to pay and get paid, tools nobody's built yet. We want to see what you make of it. AI is changing how people build, buy, sell, work, connect, and move money. Now it's your turn to imagine what comes next. Build What's Next with PayPal and AI is a global online hackathon inviting developers, designers, founders, students, and builders to create something new using PayPal and AI . There are no prescribed problem statements and no set of tracks. Build an agent, an app, an automation, a new payment experience, a business tool, a social product, or something we haven't thought of yet. The only fundamental requirement: your project must meaningfully use both PayPal and AI . Why Join? Build something ambitious — Turn an idea into a working project using PayPal and AI. Explore what’s next — Experiment with new ways people, businesses, and AI agents can interact with money and payments. Win part of $ 69,750 in total prizes — Compete for overall prizes and special awards across creativity, impact, execution, and more. Show what you can build — Put your project in front of PayPal judges, developers, and the wider hackathon community. Learn by building — Explore PayPal APIs, AI tools, agents, automations, and emerging development workflows. Build your way — Join individually or as a team, and start something new or meaningfully advance an existing project. Get started Get a PayPal Developer account (5 minutes) Review example projects and brainstorm your own (30 minutes) Webinars Oct 6th 9am PT - 9:45am PT ~ Start building with PayPal Recording Oct 7th 9am PT - 9:30am PT ~ Power Your PayPal Hackathon Project with APIMatic Context Plugins Oct 12th 7am PT - 7:45am PT ~ Build a payments dashboard without building a dashboard Oct 13th 1am PT - 2am PT ~ Start building with PayPal

title: Learn AR with SPECS
description: Design an augmented reality app for glasses, and let an AI coding agent build it in Lens Studio. You don't need the glasses, because everything runs in Lens Studio's preview on your laptop. You'll get a short concept video, a skill pack for your coding agent, a live build session, and a live project review. $2,500 in prizes each round. ABOUT THE CHALLENGE Screens won't be the only place we use computers. Glasses are coming, and building for them is different from building for a laptop or a phone. Most first tries at AR end up as a website floating in front of your face. Good AR does things a laptop can't do: It shares your view. The camera sees what you see, so the app can respond to it. It draws in the world. Content sits on the table, over the stove, at real size, right where it belongs. It leaves your body free. Your hands stay available and your eyes stay up, so you can keep doing the real thing. Coding agents can now build a working Lens from a good description. So the hard part is deciding what's worth building and how it should feel. That's what this hackathon teaches. You'll install our Devpost Learn skill pack in your coding agent. It interviews you about your idea, checks it against AR design best practices, and writes a design brief. Then Snap's CLAD agents build the Lens in Lens Studio from that brief, and you try it in the preview. You'll finish with a working Lens, the plan behind it, and a way of thinking about AR you can use on every project after this one. WHY JOIN Learn what makes a good AR app, from the design decisions an agent can't make for you. Build for SPECS, Snap's AR glasses, without owning a pair. Try Snap's newest agent tools: CLAD, the Lens Studio MCP, and LEAF testing. Get help from real people in a live build session and a live project review. Compete to win a share of $2,500. First place takes $1,250, and every winner gets a feature in the Devpost newsletter and on Devpost's socials. Everyone who submits an eligible project gets a Devpost Learn badge and a special role in the Devpost Discord. GET STARTED You'll need a computer that runs Lens Studio, Node.js and Git, and a coding agent that supports skills. Set up your tools with the quick start on the Resources tab: your coding agent, Lens Studio, the Lens Studio MCP, and the CLAD plugin. Can't sign in to the developer platform on Lens Studio 5.24? Use Lens Studio 5.23.2 instead. Watch the concept video (at the top of this page). It's short, and it covers the design ideas the judges look for. Install the skill pack: npx skills add challengepost/learn-specs --all -y. Then open your coding agent and say "Run the plan-lens skill." It takes it from there. Join the SPECS channel in the Devpost Discord for questions and to see what other builders are making. Register for the Build for SPECS: AR Design with Lens Studio and CLAD live build session on Thursday, Oct 29 at 12PM ET. We build a Lens start to finish. It's recorded if you can't make it. Come to the SPECS Live Review: Inside the Judging Criteria on Thursday, Nov 5 at 12PM ET. We review a few projects in progress against the judging criteria, so you still have time to act on the feedback before the deadline. Want yours reviewed live? Post it in the #devpost-learn-feedback channel in the Discord and tag it "Learn AR with SPECS" and "Will It Ship." Stuck? Ask in the Discord channel. Setup help, the FAQ, and event details are on the Resources tab.

title: Arbiter Hacks V1
description: About the challenge Arbiter Hacks V1 runs two parallel tracks. Pick one when you register, or switch before the submission deadline. You may only submit to one track. General Track: Build anything. Any language, any stack, any idea. This track rewards technical ambition and execution, regardless of subject. Theme Track, Rethinking Waste: Build something that helps people or systems reduce, sort, or recycle waste more effectively. Examples include a tool that identifies whether an item is recyclable, an app that routes food waste to donation, a hardware or vision system that sorts materials, or a dataset or model that improves recycling accuracy. If it moves the needle on waste, it fits. The tracks are judged separately, against separate rubrics, for separate prizes. A polished General submission and a high-impact Theme submission compete only within their own track. Get started Register and pick a track. Form a team of [1 to 4] or go solo. Late submissions are not judged.

title: UGREEN Hackathon 2026 on AI NAS
description: UGREEN is opening AI NAS to developers through UGOS and Skills Hub . Powered by UGOS , UGREEN's own Linux-based operating system, UGREEN AI NAS brings local storage, computing, and AI capabilities together in one platform. UGOS makes it easy to keep your data secure, find and organize your files, and get more done with AI. With the UGOS Skill Creation Tool and your preferred AI assistant, you can create custom Skills that use supported NAS capabilities to organize files, find information, and automate everyday tasks. UGREEN Skills Hub gives developers the freedom to explore new ideas, create innovative tools, and expand what AI NAS can do. You bring the ideas. We'll help you build them. Access developer resources and technical support, with opportunities to win prizes, gain exposure through UGREEN, and explore future collaborations. No UGREEN NAS is required to enter. Finalists will receive free access to a UGREEN AI NAS iDX6011 Pro environment for final development, testing, and validation. The Hackathon has two rounds: Round 1 (open to all): Share your idea and an early build of your Skill. You do not need a NAS to enter. Download the UGREEN Skill Developer Package. Then submit a short PDF and a Pre-test Skill Package (ZIP). Round 2 (Finalists only): UGREEN will select up to 30 Finalists. Each Finalist gets one assigned testing day of free remote access to a real UGREEN AI NAS to install, test, and polish their Skill. Finalists then submit their final Skill and a short demo video to compete for $46,000 in cash prizes! Get Started: 🧠 Get to know UGREEN AI NAS . Learn what it can do. 💬 Join the UGREEN Community . It's a place to find teammates, compare approaches, and get help when you're stuck, while keeping up with official Hackathon news and development resources and discovering community perks. ✨ 📦 Download the UGREEN Skill Developer Package . It has the tools and technical docs you need. You must use this package to build your Skill. 🛠️ Brush up on helpful skills . Python or JavaScript/TypeScript, Linux and Docker, AI agent and tool design, and file or media processing are all useful here. Why Participate 💰 Compete for $46,000 in cash prizes. Five winners will share the prize pool, including two Most Creative awards. 🚀 No NAS needed to start. Round 1 is open to everyone. You only need your idea, the Skill Developer Package, and your code . 🖥️ Test on real hardware for free. Each Finalist gets one assigned testing day of free remote access to a UGREEN AI NAS iDX6011 Pro. 🎨 Build what you care about. Choose from four tracks: work automation, personal memories, creative media, or your own original idea. 🤝 Connect with the UGREEN team. Access developer resources and technical support, with opportunities to win prizes, gain exposure through UGREEN, and explore future collaborations .

title: Codegeist 2026: Build with context. Ship with confidence.
description: What is Codegeist? Codegeist is Atlassian’s annual hackathon where developers from around the world unleash creativity on Forge, Atlassian’s serverless app development platform. By extending Atlassian products with custom apps and integrations, participants reimagine how teams plan, track, and deliver work. The Challenge AI can think. But knowing what to do – really knowing – takes context. Atlassian’s Teamwork Graph connects goals, work, people, decisions, and outcomes like associative memory for your organization, giving teams the shared understanding of who’s doing what, what’s already been decided, and what needs to happen next. That's the problem Atlassian is built to solve. And it's the problem we're inviting you to tackle. Build an app on Atlassian’s Forge platform that uses that context to help teams ship with confidence – whether that’s surfacing the right knowledge at the right moment, connecting work across silos, or turning organizational data into a decision that actually moves work forward. Join the live Build Session Tue, Nov 17, 12:00 to 12:45 PM ET on Zoom. Danny Thompson, Senior Developer Advocate at Atlassian, and Adam Moore, Group Product Manager, Forge, show how to build AI workflows with Atlassian Forge and Rovo, followed by live Q&A. Set up Forge first and you can build along. The recording will be on YouTube afterward. Register for the Build Session

title: Kiroween 2026
description: 🎃 Kiroween 2026 is open for hacking👻 Kiro’s annual Halloween-themed hackathon has returned, and building starts now. Last year, thousands of developers used Kiro to bring dead tech back to life, stitch together unexpected technologies, and create hauntingly good experiences. This year, it’s your turn. Show us how you use Kiro to push boundaries. Work across a crew of agents in Kiro Crew, add structure with specs, customize workflows with hooks or steering, streamline with Kiro powers, or bring in new capabilities with MCP. Pick a category, build something wicked, and compete for $100,000 in prizes. You have until Friday, December 4, 2026 at 2:00 PM Pacific Time to submit. Only new projects are eligible . You must build your project during the Submission Period (October 30 to December 4, 2026). Projects you started before October 30, including Kiroween 2025 projects, are not eligible. Get started Read the Official Rules . Review them before you start to build. Get free Kiro credits . Request 4,000 free Kiro credits on the Resources tab by December 1 at 12:00 pm PT. Find details on the Resources tab . Join the Kiro Discord . Get help from the Kiro team, Kiro ambassadors, and other participants in #kiroween-hackathon. You’ll also find biweekly office hours and other live events to help you along the way. Find your teammates . Browse the Participants tab (optional). Teams can have up to three members. Join the Devpost Build Session on November 11 at 10:00 AM PT. Sign up here . Start your submission early . Click “Enter a Submission” and save drafts as often as you like.

title: Meta VR Start Developer Competition 2026
description: THE META VR START DEVELOPER COMPETITION IS BACK! This year’s eight-week challenge calls on Start program members to build the next generation of Entertainment, Gaming, and Productivity experiences for Meta VR devices – including Meta VR Glasses and Meta Quest. We’re looking for hands-first apps that make interaction more natural and gameplay more intuitive than ever before. Last year, over 2,900 developers joined the competition and delivered more than 650 submissions that pushed the boundaries of immersive technology. This year, we’re raising the bar again. Whether you’re a first-time Start developer with a breakthrough idea or a seasoned creator ready to showcase what’s possible with the latest platform capabilities, this is your moment to help redefine the future of VR. Here’s what’s waiting for you: 🤝 Build hands-first. Design experiences powered by hand interactions that feel natural, responsive, and deeply immersive—no controllers required. 🛠️ Explore new tech. Take advantage of the latest OS capabilities and device features across Meta VR Glasses and Meta Quest, accelerate your development with AI tooling, including Meta VR CLI. 🌍 Join a global community. Boost your skills through mentor programming, collaborate with fellow developers, share insights, and learn from a thriving network of experienced VR developers. 🏆 Compete for $1M in cash prizes with top prizes of $100,000. The future of VR is in your hands literally . We can’t wait to see what you build. GETTING STARTED If you’re not already a member of the Start program, apply now to join the competition.
